main:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Simulates the Google Code Jam Bathroom Stalls process for each test case and prints the final selected stall's max and min distances." main]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Read one line from standard input and convert it to an integer T, the number of test cases. RESULT T]
            [COMMAND For each test case i from 1 to T inclusive, read one raw input line, split it into whitespace-separated tokens, convert each token to an integer, and assign N to the first integer and K to the second integer. RESULT N,K]
            [COMMAND Initialize stall_occupied as a list containing True for the left sentinel, then append N False values for the empty stalls, then append True for the right sentinel. RESULT stall_occupied]
            [COMMAND Initialize Ls, Rs, Min_s, and Max_s as empty lists. RESULT Ls,Rs,Min_s,Max_s]
            [COMMAND For each stall index j from 0 to N+1 inclusive, compute initial distances: if stall_occupied[j] is True, append -1 to Ls and -1 to Rs; otherwise append j-1 to Ls and N-j to Rs. Then append min(Ls[-1], Rs[-1]) to Min_s and max(Ls[-1], Rs[-1]) to Max_s. RESULT Ls,Rs,Min_s,Max_s]
            [COMMAND Within the current test case and the k-th person iteration, select the stall index idx and compute y,z as follows. Compute maximal = max(Min_s). If Min_s.count(maximal) > 1, perform the secondary tie-break: use values = np.array(Min_s) and idxs = np.where(values == maximal)[0]; build max_of_idxs = [Max_s[j] for j in idxs]; compute max_max = max(max_of_idxs); if max_of_idxs.count(max_max) > 1, use values1 = np.array(max_of_idxs) and idxs1 = np.where(values1 == max_max)[0] and set idx = idxs[idxs1[0]]; otherwise set idx = idxs[max_of_idxs.index(max_max)]. In the no-tie case where Min_s.count(maximal) == 1, set idx = Min_s.index(maximal). Then set y = max(Ls[idx], Rs[idx]) and z = min(Ls[idx], Rs[idx]). RESULT idx,y,z]
            [COMMAND Within the same k-th person iteration, mark the selected stall as occupied by setting stall_occupied[idx] to True, and set Ls[idx], Rs[idx], Min_s[idx], and Max_s[idx] to -1. RESULT stall_occupied,Ls,Rs,Min_s,Max_s]
            [COMMAND Within the same k-th person iteration, update affected stalls to the left of idx: start leftIdx at idx-1 and, while leftIdx > 0 and stall_occupied[leftIdx] is False, set Rs[leftIdx] = idx - leftIdx - 1, Min_s[leftIdx] = min(Rs[leftIdx], Ls[leftIdx]), Max_s[leftIdx] = max(Rs[leftIdx], Ls[leftIdx]), then decrement leftIdx. RESULT Rs,Min_s,Max_s]
            [COMMAND Within the same k-th person iteration, update affected stalls to the right of idx: start rightIdx at idx+1 and, while rightIdx < N+2 and stall_occupied[rightIdx] is False, set Ls[rightIdx] = rightIdx - idx - 1, Min_s[rightIdx] = min(Rs[rightIdx], Ls[rightIdx]), Max_s[rightIdx] = max(Rs[rightIdx], Ls[rightIdx]), then increment rightIdx. RESULT Ls,Min_s,Max_s]
            [COMMAND After the k loop finishes for the current test case, print the line 'Case #i: y z' using the current i, y, and z, then flush standard output. RESULT printed_output]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
